thread.title: Charting a jagged recovery attempt, S&P 500 maintains last-ditch support - MarketWatch

author: Michael Ashbaugh
title: Charting a jagged recovery attempt, S&P 500 maintains last-ditch support - MarketWatch
text:
Editor’s Note: This is a free edition of The Technical Indicator, a daily MarketWatch subscriber newsletter. To get this column each market day, click here. 
Technically speaking, the S&P 500’s recovery attempt is intact despite a persistently volatile bigger-picture backdrop. 
On a headline basis, the S&P has narrowly maintained major support — an area roughly matching the 2017 peak — rising this week from a shaky, but thus far successful, retest. 
Before detailing the U.S. markets’ wider view, the S&P 500’s SPX, +0.29% hourly chart highlights the past two weeks. 
As illustrated, the S&P has narrowly maintained major support. 
Last week’s closing low (2,677) registered just above the 2017 close (2,673) and the index has rallied to the former range. 
On further strength, the 50-day moving average, currently 2,738, remains an inflection point. 
Meanwhile, the Dow industrials’ backdrop remains slightly softer. 
Still, the index spiked 337 points Monday, and the session close (24,875) effectively matched an inflection point at the 2017 peak (24,876).
More broadly, an inflection point spans from 24,719 to 24,876, also illustrated on the daily chart. The Dow’s retest remains underway. 
Against this backdrop, the Nasdaq Composite remains the strongest major benchmark.
The index has thus far maintained its 50-day moving average on a closing basis, an area matching trendline support, illustrated below. 
Widening the view to six months adds perspective. 
On this wider view, the Nasdaq has rallied from trendline support closely matching the 50-day moving average, currently 7,194.
This area remains a bull-bear inflection point, and its recovery attempt is intact barring a violation. Delving slightly deeper, the Nasdaq has not closed under the 20-day moving average, currently 7,180, since Feb. 14.
Looking elsewhere, the Dow industrials’ backdrop remains comparably softer. 
In its case, the index has violated the 50-day moving average, currently 25,280, an area defining Nasdaq support. 
More immediately, the Dow has nailed its breakdown point from underneath (24,876), closing Monday within one point. This area defines the immediate technical tension, and a close higher would strengthen the backdrop. 
Meanwhile, the S&P 500 has survived a headline technical test. At least so far. 
Recall that last week’s close (2,691) registered within the support band broadly spanning from 2,673 to 2,695. The S&P has subsequently followed through higher, preserving an admittedly jagged recovery attempt. 
The bigger picture Broadly speaking, the major U.S. benchmarks have diverged slightly against the backdrop of a volatile March start. The prevailing technicals are not one-size-fits all. 
Moving to the small-caps, the iShares Russell 2000 ETF IWM, +0.89% has reached its latest test of familiar resistance. 
Recall that the flatlining 50-day moving average, currently 153.95, is closely followed by the breakdown point, circa 155.50. 
The small-cap benchmark has closed fractionally lower, amid decreased volume, though the retest remains underway. 
Similarly, the S&P MidCap 400 remains capped by resistance closely matching the 50-day moving average. 
Still, the prevailing upturn punctuates a successful test of support, an area spanning from about 334.90 to 335.70. 
More broadly, the small- and mid-cap benchmarks are in flux, consolidating between the 50- and 200-day moving averages. 
Meanwhile, the SPDR Trust S&P 500 is retesting its trendline, a level closely tracking the 50-day moving average, currently 273.30.
Delving slightly deeper, three inflection points stand out: 
The 20-day moving average, currently 269.70. Support matching the late-February low of 269.64. Support matching the 2017 peak of 268.60. Combined, the SPY is traversing cluttered technical territory, though its recovery attempt gets the benefit of the doubt pending a violation of support. 
Summing up the backdrop All told, the bigger-picture market technicals are not one-size-fits-all. 
On a headline basis, the Nasdaq Composite is acting relatively well, maintaining its trendline, while the small- and mid-caps continue to lag behind. 
Against this backdrop, the S&P 500 has thus far survived a notable technical test. 
Specifically, the index has narrowly maintained support spanning from 2,673 to 2,695, levels matching the December and January breakout points. 
To be sure, the prevailing backdrop remains jagged, and far from picture-perfect, though the S&P 500’s recovery attempt is intact barring a violation.
See also: Charting a bullish market backdrop as February volatility spike fades. 
Tuesday’s Watch List The charts below detail names that are technically well positioned. These are radar screen names — sectors or stocks poised to move in the near term. For the original comments on the stocks below, see The Technical Indicator Library. 
Drilling down further, the VanEck Vectors Semiconductor ETF SMH, +1.40% is acting well technically. 
As illustrated, the shares have recently maintained major support, circa 95, rising to challenge well-defined resistance. 
The range top matches record territory (109.14) and is currently under siege. An intermediate-term target projects to the 121 area on follow-through. 
Separately, consider that the early-March market downturn registers as a shallow pullback for the SMH, underpinned by the 50-day moving average. The group’s relative strength positions it to outperform once the broad markets stabilize. 
Initially profiled Feb. 15, Twitter, Inc. TWTR, +0.03% remains well positioned. 
Technically, the shares have recently gapped to two-year highs, rising after the company’s fourth-quarter results. 
The ensuing pullback has been flat, underpinned by the top of the gap, positioning the shares to build on the February spike. A near-term target projects to the 37.50 area on follow-through. 
Tableau Software, Inc. DATA, -1.72% is a well positioned large-cap name. 
The shares initially spiked four weeks ago, gapping to two-year highs after the company’s quarterly results. 
The subsequent pullback has been underpinned by the trendline, and more recently, support matching the top of the November and February gaps. 
This is a continuation pattern. A break from the prevailing range opens the path to less-charted territory — illustrated on the three-year chart — and potentially material follow-through. 
TJX Companies, Inc. TJX, +0.42% is a large-cap retailer operating stores including the T.J. Maxx, Marshalls and HomeGoods brands. 
Late last month, the shares knifed to all-time highs, gapping higher after the company’s fourth-quarter results. 
The ensuing pullback has been comparably flat, fueled by decreased volume, and underpinned by the breakout point. Tactically, a near-term floor matches the March low (81.00), and a sustained posture higher supports a bullish bias. 
Tivo, Inc. TIVO, +0.90% is a mid-cap name coming to life. 
Technically, the shares have recently cleared trendline resistance, rising after the company’s quarterly results. 
The subsequent pullback places the shares near the breakout point and 8.8% under the March peak. Tactically, the 50-day moving average, currently 14.25, closely tracked the former trend, and Tivo’s recovery attempt is intact barring a violation. 
Chart Industries, Inc. GTLS, +3.18% is a mid-cap manufacturer of engineered equipment for the natural gas, energy and biomedical industries. 
As illustrated, the shares have recently knifed to three-year highs, rising amid a volume spike after the company’s fourth-quarter results. 
The ensuing pullback places the shares at an attractive entry near the breakout point and 8.5% under the February peak. More broadly, the shares are also well positioned on the four-year chart.
